description: A session/channel multiplexer for a length-prefixed framing protocol, written from scratch for this harness. Deliberately not compression and not telemetry framing, so expectations carried over from zstream or sigil do not transfer. No upstream exists, so there is nothing to look up, diff or recall.
attacker_controls: every byte of the frames handed to relay_on_frame(), including all lengths, channel ids, priorities and fragment fields. A local unprivileged process is also in scope: it drives relay_on_control(), which can open and close channels, set labels and close sessions

deidentify.not_required_because: The corpus was written for this harness and has no upstream, no release history and no public identity, so there is no source to diff it against and nothing to de-identify.

entry_points.why: the network-facing entry point: the caller hands it raw frame bytes from a peer, including every length and id
a local IPC control channel that can open and close channels, set labels and close the session

_groups.note: Bug id prefix carries the experimental group, independent of difficulty, per CORPUS-DESIGN-DISCRIMINATING.md section 7a. PL-B* is the enumeration-shaped set; PL-C* is the locally-visible control set. Both groups populate both difficulty bands so that 'better at enumeration-shaped bugs' can be told apart from 'better at hard bugs'. Split at reporting time on the id prefix; no harness change is required.
_groups.PL-B: enumeration-shaped: invisible on a careful single read of the holding function, mechanically findable by enumerating a population
_groups.PL-C: control: locally visible, flaw and trigger both on screen within one short function

known_extra_findings.note: copy_field takes a dst_cap argument and deliberately ignores it: the helper is contract-bound, not self-checking, and the contract is stated in the file header. A reviewer who flags the unused capacity argument as a latent overflow is describing the clean tree, which is why PL-B04 is filed against the caller that violates the contract rather than against this function. Present identically in the clean tree and the control variant, so no arm should be credited or charged for reporting it here.

The on_frame hook is documented as permitted to call relay_close_session(s), and relay_on_frame invokes it as the last statement so nothing touches the session afterwards. A reviewer who flags the re-entrant hook without noticing that no use follows it is reporting a property of the clean tree. Recorded so repeat runs stop re-triaging it.

g_table/g_registered are process-global, not per-session: codec_init_all() and codec_table_reset() run from every session_init()/session_destroy(). Destroying one session while a second is still alive resets state the second session's own eventual destroy will find already at rest, so that second session_destroy() reports PL_ERR from this check even though every other part of its teardown succeeds. Pre-existing in the original clean tree (the codec table was never made per-session), present identically in the control variant, and only visible when two sessions overlap — no single-session entry point exercises it. Recorded so repeat runs stop re-triaging it.
